# Library

::: {.doc-lead}
Collect references and PDFs in a library shared by your projects.
:::

<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/library.webp" data-enlarge data-caption="Browse a small demonstration collection, with metadata and organization controls beside it."><img src="/assets/media/library.webp" alt="The Flux Library workspace showing FluxLib with three demonstration references. One row is expanded into its details strip with keywords, tags and buttons such as Get PDF and Similar. The header holds the Library and World toggle, the search box, the add-by-DOI box and buttons such as Import and Zotero." width="1500" height="950" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Browse a small demonstration collection, with metadata and organization controls beside it. <a href="/docs/visual-credits.html">Visual credits</a>.</figcaption></figure>

Library is your reference manager. It manages **FluxLib**, the machine-global collection shared
by all your projects — every paper you save, its PDF, your highlights, tags, and reading
status — while each project [cites its own subset](/docs/configuration.html). The
header shows the collection and its size; everything below is the grid.

## Getting papers in {#getting-papers-in}

- **Paste a DOI or URL.** The add box in the header (*"Add by DOI or URL…"*) takes a bare DOI,
  a `doi.org` link, or **any paper's web address** — Flux reads the page's citation metadata to
  find the DOI. arXiv pages work too.
- **Web capture.** At the bottom of the Library, the **Web capture** row shows whether the
  browser extension is connected; **Set up…** walks you through installing it. From then on,
  one click on any paper page — the article *or* the PDF itself — saves it here, with its PDF
  **and its supplementary files**. See [Capturing from the web](/docs/web-capture.html).
- **Bulk import.** **Import…** reads a `.bib` or `.ris` file (Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley,
  BibTeX exports), previews what's new vs. already-known before committing, and can pull the
  PDFs a Zotero export references alongside.
- **Zotero sync.** The **Zotero** button connects FluxLib to a Zotero library through a
  [Better BibTeX](https://retorque.re/zotero-better-bibtex/) export with **Keep updated**
  ticked. From then on, anything you add in Zotero flows into FluxLib at startup, live while
  Flux is open, or on **Sync now**. The sync is one-way and additive: papers you already have
  are recognized and left untouched, and nothing is written back to Zotero. PDFs are either
  **copied** into FluxLib (the default, so FluxLib alone is a complete backup) or **linked** to
  Zotero's folder. Agents can run the same sync with `flux zotero-sync`. The
  [Zotero integration](/docs/zotero.html) guide covers setup, copying versus linking, very large
  libraries and troubleshooting.
- **The inbox folder.** Drop PDF files into `~/FluxConfig/FluxLib/pdfs_to_assign/` and Flux
  identifies each one *from its own contents* and files it under the right paper — attaching it
  to an entry that lacks a PDF, keeping it as a supplement if the paper already has one, or
  adding the paper outright. When it isn't sure, it **refuses rather than guessing**:
  unidentifiable files land in `pdfs_to_assign/_unresolved/` with a note explaining why (and
  network hiccups just leave files in place to retry). Drops are noticed automatically. The
  **Assign PDFs** button runs a scan on demand, and its count covers both sources of unfiled
  papers: the inbox, plus any [web captures](/docs/web-capture.html) still waiting in
  your downloads folder. Pressing it brings those in and files them in one go — captures move
  only then, or at startup.
- **From a World search** — see below: any result can be added with one click.

## Finding papers {#finding-papers}

The search box does three kinds of search, all as you type:

- **Plain text** matches across titles, authors, journals, years, keys, DOIs, abstracts,
  keywords, and topics. `"quoted phrases"` match exactly.
- **Fielded filters** narrow precisely, and combine (every clause must match):

  | Filter | Alias | Matches |
  |---|---|---|
  | `author:smith` | `au:` | author names |
  | `year:2021` | `yr:` | the exact year; `year:201` matches the whole decade |
  | `journal:nature` | `venue:` | journal or venue |
  | `title:cortex` | `ti:` | title |
  | `doi:10.1038` | — | DOI |
  | `abstract:reward` | `abs:` | the enriched abstract |
  | `keyword:sleep` | `kw:` | enriched keywords |
  | `topic:neuroscience` | — | enriched topics |
  | `tag:methods` | — | your tags |
  | `status:read` | `read:` | reading status: `unread`, `reading` or `read` |
  | `collection:thesis` | `coll:` | your collections |

  Quote multi-word values: `journal:"nature neuroscience"`.
- **Full text**: prefix with `ft:` to search **inside every PDF you've stored** —
  `ft:optogenetic silencing` finds the papers whose text contains those words, with
  page-numbered snippets; click a snippet to open the paper in the
  [Reader](/docs/reader.html) at that exact spot. Metadata clauses before the prefix narrow the scan
  (`author:smith ft:entropy`).

A **Filters** disclosure appears once you have tags or collections — click facets for status,
tag, and collection instead of typing them. Column headers (**Authors**, **Title**,
**Journal**, **Year**, **Cited**, **Added**) sort; click again to reverse. **Added** is the
date a paper landed in your library — its first click shows the most recent arrivals on top,
and every paper in a bulk import shares the moment the import ran.

### Searching the world {#searching-the-world}

Flip the scope toggle from **Library** to **World** to search all of OpenAlex — by keyword or
by *meaning* (semantic search), sorted by relevance, citations, or recency. Any result adds to
your library with **+ Add**. The same machinery powers **Who cites this →** and
**Similar (semantic) →** in a paper's details.

## Working the grid {#working-the-grid}

One row, many verbs — the row tooltip is a cheat sheet:

- **Click** a row to copy its citation key (`@smith2021`), ready to paste into your
  [manuscript](/docs/paper.html). With the keyboard: arrows move, **Enter** copies, **Space** ticks
  the row's checkbox, **Escape** returns to search (typing anywhere does too).
- **Ctrl+click** expands the **details strip** — abstract, topic and keyword chips, your tags
  (add and remove them here), citation count, and the connection buttons (**Who cites this**,
  **Similar**, **More by author**, **Open DOI**).
- **Ctrl+Shift+click** opens the PDF in the Reader — fetching it first if you don't have it.
- **Alt+click** opens the paper's DOI in your browser.
- The **status dot** on each row cycles unread ○ → reading ◐ → read ●.
- **Check several rows** and a bar appears: add them all to the current project, fetch their
  PDFs (**Alt+F**), tag them in one stroke, or delete them (**Alt+Delete**, with Undo).

## PDFs {#pdfs}

- The **⬇** on a row fetches an **open-access** copy (PubMed Central, Europe PMC, arXiv,
  bioRxiv — never scraping publisher sites). **Get PDFs** in the header does the whole library
  in the background, and can be cancelled mid-run.
- **Paywalled papers** go through your university library: open **⚙** (the Keys panel), set
  your institution's **EZProxy prefix**, save your credentials (stored in the OS keychain), and
  **Sign in**. After that, **Get via library ⚿** in a paper's details — and the bulk fetch —
  route through the proxy.
- Already have the file? **Add PDF…** in the details strip files a PDF you downloaded
  yourself — or just drop it in the inbox folder.
- Fetch failures show as small pills (`no DOI`, `no OA`, `failed`) on the row, with the reason
  in the row's details. To see them all together, click the header's **⬇ No PDF** filter until
  it reads **⊘ Failed** — a **Retry all** button appears beside it, which tries them again even
  though a bulk run would normally skip a known failure. (The step only appears when something
  has actually failed.)

## Enrich {#enrich}

**Enrich** in the header fills in abstracts, topics, keywords, and citation counts for the
whole library from OpenAlex/CrossRef — no account needed. (The **⚙** Keys panel accepts
optional API keys for higher rate limits, plus a "polite email" for the registries.) Enrichment
is what powers abstract/topic search, the reference lists in the Reader, and the
citing/similar lookups.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| Add box rejects a URL | The page exposes no DOI metadata → paste the DOI itself |
| `ft:` finds nothing for a paper you have | Its PDF isn't stored yet (full-text search scans stored PDFs) → fetch it with the row's **⬇** button or **Get PDFs** first |
| No abstract / topics on a paper | Not enriched yet → **Enrich** |
| Get PDFs starts but paywalled papers fail | Proxy session expired → **⚙ → Sign in**, run again |
| A dropped PDF didn't get filed | See `pdfs_to_assign/_unresolved/` — each file carries a note saying why it couldn't be identified |
